newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends firmer on corporate demand.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends firmer on corporate demand.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed firmer on Wednesday amid good local corporate demand after trading a relatively wide range.
The currency ended at US$0.6906/13 and 68.82 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 0.6891/98 and 68.63 at the opening and having traded between 0.6887 and 0.6917.
Dealers said the currency was holding up well despite a drifting Australian dollar, with good support around the 0.6890 area and sellers waiting at 0.6925-30.
They said the key factors in the near term were movements in the major currencies and domestic politics, with parliament back in session this week for the first time this year.
